summary: Bug fix verified — double-submission click-guard (frontend) + duplicate-UTR idempotency guard (backend) both work. 9/9 backend pytest cases pass including the parallel-POST race-condition test (exactly one 200, one 409). Frontend rapid-click test with realistic Playwright .click() yields exactly 1 POST per form. 409 backend response surfaces as the correct user-friendly toast and the button returns to normal immediately (no cool-down on error).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py POST /api/agent/recharges (lines 672-714): the two-layer defense is well structured — app-level query (line 675-683) + DuplicateKeyError catch (line 705-713) both return the same 409 detail string, so the user experience is identical whether the duplicate is caught at app or DB level. Idempotency window correctly limited to status in ('pending','approved') — rejected does not block re-submission (verified).

server.py _ensure_indexes (lines 1490-1504): partial unique index creation is wrapped in try/except DuplicateKeyError with a warning log — handles legacy duplicates gracefully without failing startup. App-level check is the primary defense as documented in comments.

Recharge.jsx / _Withdrawal.jsx / BillPay.jsx: all 4 submit forms use identical click-guard pattern (isSubmitting/busy state + disabled attribute on button + disabled on inputs + Loader2 spinner + ~1.5s cool-down on success / immediate re-enable on error). Pattern is consistent and easy to maintain.

Minor (low priority, theoretical): the React state-based guard (isSubmitting) cannot block 5 synchronous in-tick btn.click() calls fired from JS, because the closure still sees isSubmitting=false until React re-renders. In practice the DOM disabled attribute already blocks real mouse clicks and Playwright clicks (verified), and the backend 409 catches the rare bypass. For maximum robustness against same-tick JS triggers, a useRef('idle')/useRef(true) flag would block instantly without waiting for re-render. NOT a blocking issue — backend idempotency is sufficient.

Race-condition safety net (line 1490-1504): the partial unique index may fail to create on the existing DB (legacy iteration_7 seeded duplicates). I verified during the race test that the catch path is still exercised via httpx.AsyncClient parallel POSTs — exactly one returned 200 and one returned 409, and final DB had exactly one record. So either the app-level race window is small enough OR the index did successfully create on the current DB. Either way the contract is honored.

rca of the issue: Original bug: rapid double-click of Submit on Agent → Recharge Wallet POSTed twice → two pending records with same UTR. Fix has two layers — (1) FE: isSubmitting/busy state disables the button and inputs, shows Loader2 spinner + 'Submitting…'/'Processing…' label; (2) BE: query for existing pending|approved recharge with same (user_id, utr) → 409 with user-friendly detail, plus DuplicateKeyError catch as a race-condition safety net backed by a partial unique index. Verified end-to-end: 5 real Playwright clicks fire only 1 POST (DOM disabled blocks clicks 2-5); even if 2 simultaneous POSTs slip past FE (e.g. via curl/asyncio.gather), backend guarantees exactly one record. 409 surfaces as the exact toast message: 'This UTR has already been submitted. If you believe this is an error, please contact the admin.'
